cues.title: Welcome, and the mock-Knowledge-Box honesty rule
cues.text: Document Processing turns paperwork into a checked, structured record, and shows where every value came from. It runs against a mock Knowledge Box — and says so.

cues.title: The guided sample, and its tour
cues.text: Starting the guided sample drops a document into the queue and opens a short tour of the real screen underneath it — not a mock of the product, the product itself. The tour never blocks the page it describes.

cues.title: Upload a document worth reviewing
cues.text: To see the product prove something, I'll upload a document with a real problem in it — the accepted types and the size limit here come from the API, not from markup that could drift out of date.

cues.title: The queue: worth reviewing, worth trusting
cues.text: A supplier invoice whose subtotal and tax don't add up to the printed total. The row tells the story already: twelve fields, full grounding, one issue flagged.

cues.title: The record: a claim with a denominator
cues.text: Every record opens with this strip — never a bare percentage. 'Twelve of twelve fields carry a quote found in this document' is a claim you can check. And the subtotal and tax don't reconcile with the total — flagged automatically.

cues.title: The evidence beat: a field's own quote
cues.text: Every field carries its own quote, not just a value. Opening the evidence on Total shows exactly what was read — and the issue that quote raised sits on the field itself, not only in a banner.

cues.title: Source & evidence: the quote, in the document's own text
cues.text: This is the loop closing: the quote isn't just printed back at you, it's highlighted inside the actual text Progress Agentic RAG read from the document. Selecting a field jumps straight to its sentence — this is the difference between a system that asserts and one that shows.

cues.title: Pipeline: seven stages, real timings
cues.text: Every stage that produced this record is on the Pipeline tab, with its own timing — this is the same job the queue streamed live, available afterwards for any run.

cues.title: Export the record
cues.text: The record exports as CSV, JSON or XML — whatever the downstream ledger expects, with no re-mapping.

cues.title: Ask this document
cues.text: Because the document lives in a Knowledge Box, not just a table row, you can ask it a question directly and get an answer traced back to the same source text — not the model's general knowledge.

cues.title: A custom extraction config
cues.text: Eleven document types ship built in, but real catalogues always have one more form. Naming the fields here is the whole job — saving is what does the work.

cues.title: Saved, and provisioned
cues.text: Saving doesn't just store names — it provisions a stored search configuration that forces the model to return exactly these fields, grounded. No redeploy.

cues.title: Settings: what this deployment is connected to
cues.text: Anyone using the product can answer 'what am I actually connected to?' for themselves, here — no admin token required.

cues.title: Admin: sign in, and the operator's own view
cues.text: Operators get a separate product behind its own sign-in: live health, grounding, and a worklist of what needs attention — not a tab bolted onto the app Dana uses.

cues.title: Admin → Connection: the stored search configurations
cues.text: Every extraction config is backed by a real search configuration — model, strategy, prompt and schema — readable without the Knowledge Box dashboard.

cues.title: The API docs
cues.text: Every screen in this recording is a documented, contract-tested endpoint — there is no UI-only capability. Clone the repo, run it, and it's the same product against the same mock.
